analysis: Both changed files are test-only, so no production control changes in them. MediaIngestTests.swift: the patch updates assertions to the new `.source` accessor on decoded image/video results (`decodeImage`, `decodeVideo`, `decodeImageData`). The visible head excerpt (lines 673-815) shows tests that cover the media limits: per-request image count cap, per-image pixel cap, video frame-pixel cap, video count cap, and decoded-byte cap. These support the media DoS and plaintext-handling posture (TB-003/TB-007, T-050) and do not weaken it. One test still asserts that memory-backed video avoids plaintext temp files. QwenVLMTargetExtractionTests.swift: the only change is `try` added before `reKeyedQwenTargetWeights` (line 194). This implies the production function now throws, plausibly rejecting unexpected or mismatched keys. That is a stricter, fail-closed direction. Both the production change and the new `.source` wrapper type are outside the supplied evidence, so I could not verify them. Hence I note that the production MediaIngest changes (a new image/video wrapper type and the throwing re-key function) should be reviewed in their own source units. Specifically, check that the caps in MediaIngest.swift are still enforced on every decode path, and that the wrapper does not hold plaintext longer or write it to disk. The existing prefix-cache tests (T-041) are unchanged context; their SSD-tier, salt and receipt expectations are not modified. No regression is identifiable from these test-only changes.
